clue.text: Live to become father

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
to become is to get, as in get angry

explanation.surface: Someone survives long enough to have children of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: To father, as a verb, is to sire or produce offspring, the old biblical sense.

clue.text: Prose garbage, rewritten for the stage?

definitions.note: the definition names a work written for the theatre

indicators.note: a rewritten text has its words reworked, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Some poor prose is being adapted into a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is John Gay's 1728 ballad opera, a work for the stage, and its story of thieves fits the 'garbage' of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gay's eighteenth-century ballad opera is a famous theatrical work, hence a piece made for performance.

clue.text: So singled out for piety

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is picked out for their religious devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotion to God and holy living is the core meaning of both words.

clue.text: London tourist attraction, one exerting a pull

definitions.meaning: the historic fortress by the Thames that houses the Crown Jewels
someone who tows, hauling a load behind

explanation.surface: A London sight that draws the crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tower of London is a major sight, and read as tow-er the word means a puller.

clue.text: Nags husband foully, we hear

parts.note: a nagging wife is said to do this to her husband, and 'foully' heard aloud is 'fowl-ly': what a farmyard bird does with its beak

explanation.surface: A wife's nagging of her husband is described as nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nags husband' is the plain meaning; 'foully, we hear' sounds like 'fowl-ly', the literal picture of a bird jabbing with its beak.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife who constantly bosses and criticises her spouse is said to be doing this, an idiom from farmyard birds.

clue.text: Bash gate as one way to get out

parts.note: to bash is to hit
a wicket is a small gate

explanation.surface: Smashing a gate as a means of escape.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman is out if he knocks his own stumps (the wicket) with bat or body.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the official methods of dismissal in cricket.

clue.text: Carol and boyfriend?

definitions.meaning: a Christmas song, a seasonal carol
a male first name, so a possible boyfriend for a girl called Carol

explanation.surface: A woman named Carol and her partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a girl's name; it is a Christmas song, and the boyfriend is a man with the matching festive name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas song has this French-derived name, which is also a man's first name.

clue.text: Old taxi worker in high spirits

parts.note: ex means former, old
Uber is a ride-hailing taxi service
a worker ant, the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A former cab driver is in a cheerful mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bubbling over with energy and cheerfulness is lively and full of high spirits.

clue.text: 3s, for which one has permanent possession

definitions.meaning: the plural of the answer to 3 down: strong central buildings of castles

definitions.text: for which one has permanent possession
definitions.meaning: something won 'for ...' is yours forever, never returned

explanation.surface: A cross-reference and a description of ownership for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Castle strongholds have this name, and the idiom for good and forever completes the phrase 'for ...'.

clue.text: Completely fail to take the Underground, son?

parts.note: the Tube is London's Underground railway, so taking it is going down the tube

explanation.surface: A question about whether a son should travel by London's Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'go down the tubes' means to collapse or be ruined entirely.

clue.text: Cheat who hands out too many cards?

definitions.text: who hands out too many cards?
definitions.meaning: a card dealer who deals twice the right amount

explanation.surface: A card sharp who deals extra cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-faced deceiver is called this, and read literally it is a dealer who deals double.

clue.text: Pollutant in a Jersey ditch?

parts.note: Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI
a drain is a channel or ditch carrying water away

explanation.surface: Something polluting has been found in a ditch on the island of Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is a British island in the English Channel, one of the Channel Islands (CI).
explanation.definitionFit: Rainfall made acidic by industrial emissions is a well-known form of environmental pollution.

clue.text: Encouragement to start releases

definitions.meaning: a cry urging people to get moving, like 'come on, off we go'
to release something is to stop holding it, to let it loose

explanation.surface: A cheer to get things moving, and something being set free.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a rallying call to begin and a verb phrase meaning frees from one's grip.

clue.text: Shin keeps itching in fleece

indicators.note: itching suggests restless twitching, so the letters of these two words wriggle into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's shin keeps itching inside a woolly fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece is the woolly coat of a sheep, and its tanned hide with wool on is the same thing.

clue.text: Time for a friendly game of football

definitions.text: Time for a friendly game of football

parts.words: Time for a friendly game of football
parts.note: warm-up matches that do not count, called friendlies, are played before the league campaign begins

explanation.surface: Asking when to have a casual kickabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friendly' is the football term for a non-competitive match, not a description of the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The weeks before the competitive football calendar starts are when clubs play warm-up friendlies.

clue.text: Muse tends to confuse — it's inevitable

indicators.note: to confuse things is to jumble them, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A poet's inspiration always muddles them, and nothing can be done.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'needs must when the devil drives' says one is compelled to act; there is no avoiding it.

clue.text: One bald unexpected remark

indicators.note: something unexpected comes out in a surprising form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A bald person makes a surprising comment.
explanation.definitionFit: An improvised, unscripted comment is called by this Latin-derived term meaning at pleasure.

clue.text: Details not finalised, so one's led into error

indicators.note: being led into error means going astray, so these letters go into a wrong order

explanation.surface: Unfinished details cause someone to make a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Unresolved matters left hanging at the end of a project are known by this idiom.

clue.text: Spread over Spain

parts.note: over means finished, past
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Something spreads across the whole of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth paste such as fish paste is a spread for bread.

clue.text: Take an age to score a single

parts.note: a score is twenty
a single is one

explanation.surface: A slow batsman takes forever to score a single run in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Being this many years old was traditionally the age of majority, coming of age.

clue.text: Popular artist's cover announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out loud, so the word for cover is heard rather than written

parts.note: a wrapper is a cover, as round a sweet

explanation.surface: A pop star's album cover is unveiled.
explanation.definitionFit: A hip-hop performer is a popular musical artist.

clue.text: Sort of finish picture

definitions.meaning: a race result decided by a camera at the line is a ... finish

explanation.surface: A type of ending, and an image.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera-judged close race is a ... finish, and a snapshot is a picture.

clue.text: A small cat, not one from an Indian state

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: not says the following piece is left out of the cat breed

parts.note: a Siamese is a breed of cat
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A little cat that does not come from a particular Indian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes I (one) from SIAMESE, leaving SAMESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a state in north-east India, and the adjective describes its people, language or tea.

clue.text: Poor Lear, interrupted by one from another play

indicators.note: interrupted means broken into, so the next piece goes inside the jumbled letters
poor means badly made, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's tragic King Lear meets a character from a different play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' scrambles LEAR into AREL; 'interrupted by' puts I inside it. Lear is itself a play, so the answer comes from another one: The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: The airy spirit serving Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest is a character from a play other than King Lear.

clue.text: Sound sad, vision being cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: sight is the faculty of vision

explanation.surface: Sounding sad because one's eyesight is failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting out a long audible breath is the noise one makes when sorrowful or weary.

clue.text: Promenade in accordance with law

definitions.meaning: a promenade is a leisurely walk taken for health
allowed by the fundamental laws of a state

explanation.surface: A seaside walk and something permitted by law.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk walk for one's health has this old name, and the adjective means lawful under a nation's founding charter.

clue.text: Wanders listlessly, very keen for space travel

parts.note: to moon about is to wander around listlessly
hot means very keen or eager, as in hot on

explanation.surface: Someone drifts aimlessly yet is passionate about going into space.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch aimed at reaching the Moon is a classic example of a journey beyond Earth.

clue.text: Such surgery scares a lot — not all coming back

indicators.note: coming back says the hidden letters are read backwards
not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some kinds of surgery frighten many patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Operations using a concentrated light beam are a common type of modern eye surgery.
